From 8b07e990fb254fcbaa919616ac77f981cb48c73d Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Iwona Winiarska <iwona.winiarska@intel.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2021 01:48:19 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] soc: aspeed: p2a-ctrl: Fix boundary check for mmap

The check mixes pages (vm_pgoff) with bytes (vm_start, vm_end) on one
side of the comparison, and uses resource address (rather than just the
resource size) on the other side of the comparison.
This can allow malicious userspace to easily bypass the boundary check and
map pages that are located outside memory-region reserved by the driver.

Fixes: 01c60dcea9f7 ("drivers/misc: Add Aspeed P2A control driver")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Iwona Winiarska <iwona.winiarska@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Andrew Jeffery <andrew@aj.id.au>
Tested-by: Andrew Jeffery <andrew@aj.id.au>
Reviewed-by: Joel Stanley <joel@aj.id.au>
Signed-off-by: Joel Stanley <joel@jms.id.au>

diff --git a/drivers/soc/aspeed/aspeed-p2a-ctrl.c b/drivers/soc/aspeed/aspeed-p2a-ctrl.c
index b60fbeaffcbd..20b5fb2a207c 100644
--- a/drivers/soc/aspeed/aspeed-p2a-ctrl.c
+++ b/drivers/soc/aspeed/aspeed-p2a-ctrl.c
@@ -110,7 +110,7 @@ static int aspeed_p2a_mmap(struct file *file, struct vm_area_struct *vma)
 	vsize = vma->vm_end - vma->vm_start;
 	prot = vma->vm_page_prot;
 
-	if (vma->vm_pgoff + vsize > ctrl->mem_base + ctrl->mem_size)
+	if (vma->vm_pgoff + vma_pages(vma) > ctrl->mem_size >> PAGE_SHIFT)
 		return -EINVAL;
 
 	/* ast2400/2500 AHB accesses are not cache coherent */
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/soc/aspeed/aspeed-p2a-ctrl.c`**
- The boundary check in the `aspeed_p2a_mmap` function has been modified. 
- The original condition checked if the sum of `vma->vm_pgoff` and `vsize` (the size of the memory area) exceeded the sum of `ctrl->mem_base` and `ctrl->mem_size`.
- The modified condition now checks if the sum of `vma->vm_pgoff` and the number of pages in the virtual memory area (`vma_pages(vma)`) exceeds half of `ctrl->mem_size` (after right-shifting by `PAGE_SHIFT`).

### Relationships Between Modifications
- The change addresses a security vulnerability where the original boundary check could allow userspace to map memory pages outside the reserved memory region. 
- By correcting the comparison to use the correct units (pages instead of bytes) and focusing solely on the resource size, the patch enhances the integrity of memory mapping operations, ensuring that only valid memory regions are accessible to userspace. 
- This modification is crucial for maintaining the security and stability of the driver, preventing potential exploitation by malicious users.

soc: aspeed: p2a-ctrl: Fix boundary check for mmap

The check mixes pages (vm_pgoff) with bytes (vm_start, vm_end) on one
side of the comparison, and uses resource address (rather than just the
resource size) on the other side of the comparison.
This can allow malicious userspace to easily bypass the boundary check and
map pages that are located outside memory-region reserved by the driver.

Fixes: 01c60dcea9f7 ("drivers/misc: Add Aspeed P2A control driver")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Iwona Winiarska <iwona.winiarska@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Andrew Jeffery <andrew@aj.id.au>

Here is the root cause:
The bug arises from a flawed boundary check in the `aspeed_p2a_mmap` function, where the comparison incorrectly mixes page offsets with byte sizes, allowing userspace to potentially map memory pages outside the reserved region by bypassing the check. This misalignment in units (pages vs. bytes) and the use of resource address instead of just the resource size creates a security vulnerability.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int aspeed_p2a_mmap(struct file *file, struct vm_area_struct *vma)
 {
 	unsigned long vsize;
 	pgprot_t prot;
 	struct aspeed_p2a_user *priv = file->private_data;
 	struct aspeed_p2a_ctrl *ctrl = priv->parent;
 
 	if (ctrl->mem_base == 0 && ctrl->mem_size == 0)
 		return -EINVAL;
 
 	vsize = vma->vm_end - vma->vm_start;
 	prot = vma->vm_page_prot;
 
-	if (vma->vm_pgoff + vsize > ctrl->mem_base + ctrl->mem_size)
+	if (vma->vm_pgoff + vma_pages(vma) > ctrl->mem_size >> PAGE_SHIFT)
 		return -EINVAL;
 
 	/* ast2400/2500 AHB accesses are not cache coherent */
 	prot = pgprot_noncached(prot);
 
 	if (remap_pfn_range(vma, vma->vm_start,
 		(ctrl->mem_base >> PAGE_SHIFT) + vma->vm_pgoff,
 		vsize, prot))
 		return -EAGAIN;
 
 	return 0;
 }
